answer.rationale: The line runs at 94% of committed volume with no buffer and the contract expires in 14 days, so switching the primary vendor (per memory_c2's low-cost claim, which I want verified against the original record) risks delivery interruption exactly when there is no slack. The 18% spend-cut mandate points to the renewal negotiation lever: memory_c4 shows benchmarking moved the incumbent on price and terms, and memory_c6 shows multi-year commitments unlocked volume pricing. Negotiating terms at this renewal targets the mandated savings while keeping the stable integration (memory_c1) and avoiding delivery risk. I verify c2 and c4 because those two records most directly determine whether a switch or a renegotiation is the better cost lever; if c4's margin recovery proves weaker than remembered or c2's savings larger and cleaner, the intended action changes. Deferral is rejected because the contract does not auto-renew and there is no buffer.
